messages.subject: sort dataframe
parts:
I have a dataframe that looks like following:

df <- data.frame(
  v1=c(NA, 'adult (10)', 'juv (20)', 'male adult (40)', 
       'female adult (10)', 'male juv (30)', 
       'female juv (20)'),
  stringsAsFactors=FALSE)

I need the values extracted from v1, and placed in separate columns. The dataframe I need is as follows:

dfNeeded <- data.frame(
  adult= c(NA, 10, 0, 40, 10, 0, 0), 
    juv= c(NA, 0, 20, 0, 0, 30, 20),
    male= c(NA, 0, 0, 40, 0, 30, 0),
    female=c(NA, 0, 0, 0, 10, 0, 20))

Is this a task for reshape?

This is first a task for some string manipulation in order to identify
who is adult, age, etc. For that, you can look at ?strsplit but more
like you will want to use some regular expression mojo -- which you
can start reading about in ?regexpr

The stringr package might also be useful for you:

https://hedgehog.fhcrc.org/bioconductor/trunk/madman/Rpacks/ReportingTools

After you parse your data "correctly", reshape might then be useful.

HTH,

On 1/26/2013 9:59 AM, Ross Ahmed wrote:
> I have a dataframe that looks like following:
>
> df <- data.frame(
> v1=c(NA, 'adult (10)', 'juv (20)', 'male adult (40)',
> 'female adult (10)', 'male juv (30)',
> 'female juv (20)'),
> stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
>
> I need the values extracted from v1, and placed in separate columns. The
> dataframe I need is as follows:
>
> dfNeeded <- data.frame(
> adult= c(NA, 10, 0, 40, 10, 0, 0),
> juv= c(NA, 0, 20, 0, 0, 30, 20),
> male= c(NA, 0, 0, 40, 0, 30, 0),
> female=c(NA, 0, 0, 0, 10, 0, 20))
>
> Is this a task for reshape?

Not really. reshape is for changing a data.frame which from wide to long
or vice versa. This is "just" string manipulation, as Steve described.

library("plyr") # for mutate function
dfNeeded <- mutate(df,
n = as.numeric(gsub(".*\\((\\d+)\\)", "\\1", v1)),
adult = ifelse(grepl("adult", v1)|is.na(v1), n, 0),
juv = ifelse(grepl("juv", v1)|is.na(v1), n, 0),
male = ifelse(grepl("male", v1)|is.na(v1), n, 0),
female = ifelse(grepl("female", v1)|is.na(v1), n, 0))


> dfNeeded
v1 n adult juv male female
1 <NA> NA NA NA NA NA
2 adult (10) 10 10 0 0 0
3 juv (20) 20 0 20 0 0
4 male adult (40) 40 40 0 40 0
5 female adult (10) 10 10 0 10 10
6 male juv (30) 30 0 30 30 0
7 female juv (20) 20 0 20 20 20

The regexp for n pulls out digits within parentheses; the others look
for specific words and give either 0 or what was computed for n as the
return, which gives what you described.
